title: Authentication Failures Across Multiple Accounts From One Source
detection_hypothesis: If a single source sprays credentials, the number of distinct target accounts failing from that source will rise sharply while per-account failure counts stay low.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.IpAddress: Network address associated with the authentication attempt.

collection_prerequisites: Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
ingestion_differences: Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
expected_volume: Low; sensitive to the distinct account threshold.
false_positive_strategy: Shared egress addresses are the main source of benign matches. Tune by excluding documented gateway addresses from the group key and by raising the distinct account threshold for those sources.
tuning_guidance: Prefer raising the threshold for known gateways over removing the source entirely, so that a genuine spray from behind the gateway is still visible.
test_strategy: Positive sequences fail five or more distinct accounts from one address. Negative sequences repeat one account, spread across two addresses, and stay under the threshold.
